committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects Department of Homeland Security personnel, intelligence community detailees, federal agencies, and federal, state, local, and tribal partners participating in fusion centers.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of Homeland Security shall establish in the Department of Homeland Security a working group

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an interagency-coordinated working group, research and development testing programs, and mandatory annual unclassified reports to Congress regarding national security threats.
dimensions.evidence: carry out research and development, including operational testing, of technologies and techniques for enhancing the Department's security and situational awareness

dimensions.assessment: Requires allocation of existing DHS department resources and staffing for the working group and research and development activities, without specifying a new funding appropriation.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of Homeland Security shall ensure the Working Group is provided with a sufficient number of employees

dimensions.assessment: Directs broad internal DHS reorganization and assessment duties covering immigration system exploitation, trade practices, illicit finance, and information sharing through the National Network of Fusion Centers.
dimensions.evidence: Examine, assess, and report upon efforts by the Department of Homeland Security to counter terrorist, cybersecurity, border and port security, and transportation security threats

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a temporary program structure with annual reporting requirements over a five-year period, culminating in a mandatory sunset seven years after establishment.
dimensions.evidence: The Working Group shall terminate on the date that is seven years after the establishment of the Working Group

missing_information: Specific dollar amounts allocated from existing DHS budgets to fund the working group and R&D activities.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates the establishment of a Department of Homeland Security working group to counter threats from the Chinese Communist Party across immigration, trade, and financial activities, requiring annual public reports, research and development, and a 7-year sunset.
